arxiv-2011-03303.title: Deep coastal sea elements forecasting using U-Net based models Journal: arXiv
arxiv-2011-03303.creator: Jesús García Fernández, Ismail Alaoui Abdellaoui, Siamak Mehrkanoon
arxiv-2011-03303.description: Abstract The supply and demand of energy is influenced by meteorological conditions. The relevance of accurate weather forecasts increases as the demand for renewable energy sources increases. The energy providers and policy makers require weather information to make informed choices and establish optimal plans according to the operational objectives.

arxiv-2203-08819.title: Hierarchical Clustering and Matrix Completion for the Reconstruction of World Input-Output Tables Journal: AStA Advances in Statistical Analysis
arxiv-2203-08819.creator: Rodolfo Metulini, Giorgio Gnecco, Francesco Biancalani, Massimo Riccaboni
arxiv-2203-08819.description: Abstract World Input-Output (I/O) matrices provide the networks of within- and cross-country economic relations. In the context of I/O analysis, the methodology adopted by national statistical offices in data collection raises the issue of obtaining reliable data in a timely fashion and it makes the reconstruction of (part of) the I/O matrices of particular interest.

arxiv-2207-06714.title: A Comprehensive Analysis of the Gravitational Wave Events with the Hilbert-Huang Transform: From Compact Binary Coalescence to Supernova Matlab ( MATLAB 2018 ) , Python3 ( Van Rossum & Drake 2009 ) , GWpy ( Macleod et al. 2020 ) , PyCBC ( Usman et al. 2016 )
arxiv-2207-06714.creator: Chin-Ping Hu, Lupin Chun-Che Lin, Kuo-Chuan Pan, Kwan-Lok Li, Chien-Chang Yen, Albert K. H. Kong, C. Y. Hui
arxiv-2207-06714.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Chin-Ping Hu, Lupin Chun-Che Lin, Kuo-Chuan Pan, Kwan-Lok Li, Chien-Chang Yen, Albert K. H. Kong, C. Y. Hui. We analyze the gravitational wave signals with a model-independent time-frequency analysis, which is improved from the Hilbert-Huang transform (HHT) and optimized for characterizing the frequency variability on the time-frequency map. Except for the regular HHT algorithm, i.e., obtaining intrinsic mode functions with ensemble empirical mode decomposition and yielding the instantaneous frequencies, we propose an alternative algorithm that operates the ensemble mean on the time-frequency map.

arxiv-2212-12384.title: Convergence rate analysis of randomized and cyclic coordinate descent for convex optimization through semidefinite programming
arxiv-2212-12384.creator: Hadi Abbaszadehpeivasti 1 , Etienne de Klerk 1,∗ , Moslem Zamani 1
arxiv-2212-12384.description: Abstract 1 Tilburg University, Department of Econometrics and Operations Research, Tilburg, The Netherlands Abstract. In this paper, we study randomized and cyclic coordinate descent for convex unconstrained optimization problems. We improve the known convergence rates in some cases by using the numerical semidefinite programming performance estimation method.

arxiv-2305-01907.title: Comparison of new computational methods for geostatistical modelling of malaria
arxiv-2305-01907.creator: Spencer Wong, Jennifer A. Flegg, Nick Golding, Sevvandi Kandanaarachchi
arxiv-2305-01907.description: Abstract Background Geostatistical analysis of health data is increasingly used to model spatial variation in malaria prevalence, burden, and other metrics. Traditional inference methods for geostatistical modelling are notoriously computationally intensive, motivating the development of newer, approximate methods. The appeal of faster methods is particularly great as the size of the region and number of spatial locations being modelled increases.

arxiv-2305-09305.title: Releasing Inequality Phenomena in L ∞ L_{\infty} -Adversarial Training via Input Gradient Distillation
arxiv-2305-09305.creator: Junxi Chen, Junhao Dong, Xiaohua Xie
arxiv-2305-09305.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Junxi Chen, Junhao Dong, Xiaohua Xie. Since adversarial examples appeared and showed the catastrophic degradation they brought to DNN, many adversarial defense methods have been devised, among which adversarial training is considered the most effective. However, a recent work showed the inequality phenomena in l ∞ l_{\infty} -adversarial training and revealed that the l ∞ l_{\infty} -adversarially trained model is vulnerable when a few important pixels are perturbed by i.i.d.

arxiv-2306-04983.title: Fundamental Limitations on Communication over a Quantum Network
arxiv-2306-04983.creator: Junjing Xing, Tianfeng Feng, Zhaobing Fan, Haitao Ma, Kishor Bharti, Dax Enshan Koh, Yunlong Xiao
arxiv-2306-04983.description: Abstract Entanglement, a fundamental feature of quantum mechanics, has long been recognized as a valuable resource in enabling secure communications and surpassing classical limits. However, previous research has primarily concentrated on static entangled states generated at a single point in time, overlooking the crucial role of the quantum dynamics responsible for creating such states.

arxiv-2401-02457.title: eCIL-MU: Embedding based Class Incremental Learning and Machine Unlearning
arxiv-2401-02457.creator: Zhiwei Zuo, Zhuo Tang, Bin Wang, Kenli Li, Anwitaman Datta
arxiv-2401-02457.description: Abstract New categories may be introduced over time, or existing categories may need to be reclassified. Class incremental learning (CIL) is employed for the gradual acquisition of knowledge about new categories while preserving information about previously learned ones in such dynamic environments.

arxiv-2407-03878.title: Geodesic Optimization for Predictive Shift Adaptation on EEG data
arxiv-2407-03878.creator: Apolline Mellot, Antoine Collas, Sylvain Chevallier, Alexandre Gramfort, Denis A. Engemann
arxiv-2407-03878.description: Abstract Electroencephalography (EEG) data is often collected from diverse contexts involving different populations and EEG devices. This variability can induce distribution shifts in the data X X and in the biomedical variables of interest y y , thus limiting the application of supervised machine learning (ML) algorithms.

arxiv-2411-11159.title: Federated Learning for UAV-Based Spectrum Sensing: Enhancing Accuracy Through SNR-Weighted Model Aggregation
arxiv-2411-11159.creator: Kürşat Tekbıyık 1 , Güneş Karabulut Kurt 1 , Antoine Lesage-Landry 2
arxiv-2411-11159.description: Abstract The increasing demand for data usage in wireless communications requires using wider bands in the spectrum, especially for backhaul links. Yet, allocations in the spectrum for non-communication systems inhibit merging bands to achieve wider bandwidth. To overcome this issue, spectrum-sharing or opportunistic spectrum utilization by secondary users stands out as a promising solution.

pmc-10631184.title: Bullying behaviors and intention to drop-out among nursing students: the mediation roles of sense of belonging and major satisfaction
pmc-10631184.creator: Hamid Sharif-Nia, João Marôco, Pardis Rahmatpour, Kelly A Allen, Omolhoda Kaveh, Esmaeil Hoseinzadeh
pmc-10631184.description: Bullying in academic settings has long-lasting implications on students’ well-being and career prospects, particularly in fields like nursing that require a high level of interpersonal skills and emotional resilience. This study explored the relationships between experiences of bullying and intentions to drop out among Iranian nursing students, with major satisfaction and a sense of belonging serving as mediating factors.

pmc-10632516.title: Expression of a large coding sequence: Gene therapy vectors for Ataxia Telangiectasia
pmc-10632516.creator: Tanja Hirch, Nadine Brander, Franziska Schenk, Simon J. Pöllmann, Janine Reichenbach, Ralf Schubert, Ute Modlich
pmc-10632516.description: Ataxia telangiectasia is a monogenetic disorder caused by mutations in the ATM gene. Its encoded protein kinase ATM plays a fundamental role in DNA repair of double strand breaks (DSBs). Impaired function of this kinase leads to a multisystemic disorder including immunodeficiency, progressive cerebellar degeneration, radiation sensitivity, dilated blood vessels, premature aging and a predisposition to cancer.

pmc-11312884.title: Exercise-Induced Bronchoconstriction in Children: State of the Art from Diagnosis to Treatment
pmc-11312884.creator: Roberto Grandinetti, Nicole Mussi, Arianna Rossi, Giulia Zambelli, Marco Masetti, Antonella Giudice, Simone Pilloni, Michela Deolmi, Carlo Caffarelli, Susanna Esposito, Valentina Fainardi, Roberto Gasparri
pmc-11312884.description: Exercise-induced bronchoconstriction (EIB) is a common clinical entity in people with asthma. EIB is characterized by postexercise airway obstruction that results in symptoms such as coughing, dyspnea, wheezing, chest tightness, and increased fatigue. The underlying mechanism of EIB is not completely understood. “Osmotic theory” and “thermal or vascular theory” have been proposed.

pmc-11354356.title: Anti-Neuroinflammatory Effect of Ombuin from Rhamnus erythroxylon Pall. Leaves in LPS-Induced BV-2 Microglia by Targeting Src and Suppressing the PI3K-AKT/NF-κB Signaling Pathway
pmc-11354356.creator: Yanjie Bian, Nan Qiao, Suyun Han, Jixiang Gao, Xiaofang Lv, Lihuan Yuan, Linjing Zhang, Zuofu Wei
pmc-11354356.description: The leaves of Rhamnus erythroxylon Pall. are widely used as tea substitutes in northwest China for their fragrant aroma, anti-irritability, and digestion-enhancing properties. Ombuin, a main flavonoid compound found in the leaves, exhibited notable anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects. However, its potential role in treating neuroinflammatory-related diseases remains unexplored.

pmc-11607070.title: Non-contact measurement method of liquid composition using microwave radar cross-section
pmc-11607070.creator: Weijia Zhang, Xuejing Cao, Xue Cheng, Tianfang Wei, Dongqin Sun, Zhaowei Wang, Nutapong Somjit, Calvin Choi, Shaomin Cai
pmc-11607070.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This study aims to provide a non-contact detection of liquid composition inside containers using Microwave Radar Cross-section (RCS) measurement technology. Firstly, it analyzes the limitations of traditional near-infrared spectroscopy methods and proposes the necessity of introducing microwave detection methods. The research demonstrates through experiments a significant correlation between polar substances like total acid content and radar scattering capability, showing microwave radar’s effectiveness in reflecting the polarity characteristics of liquids.

pmc-13011730.title: Syndromic surveillance systems to detect outbreaks of gastroenteritis in high-income countries: a scoping review
pmc-13011730.creator: Faris Adel Mutawalli, Amalie Dyda, Satyamurthy Anuradha, Sheleigh Lawler, Phu Cong Do, Rehab Meckawy, Simon Reid
pmc-13011730.description: BackgroundSyndromic surveillance systems leverage non-diagnostic data sources to enable the early detection of infectious gastroenteritis outbreaks. However, their use in high-income countries (HICs) remains underexplored. This scoping review explores published literature on syndromic surveillance for gastroenteritis outbreaks in HICs, focusing on the types of data used, their effectiveness, and reported outcomes.

pmc-13019415.title: A Systematic Review With Targeted Meta-Analyses of Curcumin and Berberine In Vitro Cytotoxicity Models (2014-2026)
pmc-13019415.creator: Suresh K, Saravanasingh Karan Chand Mohan Singh, Shalini Boopathi, Sugumaran P Pichamuthu, Nithyamala I, Gayatri R
pmc-13019415.description: Traditional systems of medicine (siddha, ayurveda, and traditional Chinese medicine (TCM)) contribute a large fraction of natural products investigated for anticancer activity. Yet quantitative synthesis is often invalidated by extreme methodological heterogeneity (different cell lines, exposure times, and viability assays).

pmc-13472889.title: Glutamate excitatory inputs to the sublaterodorsal tegmental nucleus are necessary for REM sleep—where are they located?
pmc-13472889.creator: Steven Ngo, Gerard Kim, HanHee Lee, Anita Taksokhan, John Peever, Jimmy J Fraigne

pmc-13676498.title: Histotype and molecular subtype integration in epithelial ovarian cancer: implications for targeted treatment
pmc-13676498.creator: Shuyi Liu, Chaoyang Sun
pmc-13676498.description: Ovarian cancer remains a major global health burden among women, ranking eighth in both cancer incidence and cancer mortality worldwide in 2024, with an estimated 330,731 new cases and 203,850 deaths. Epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) accounts for more than 90% of ovarian cancers and comprises five major histological subtypes with distinct biological behavior, molecular alterations, and therapeutic vulnerabilities.
